title: Children's dental treatment under general anesthesia
what: Your child sleeps under general anesthesia while the dentist treats all the bad teeth at once. An anesthetist is there the whole time.
why: When there are many bad teeth, the child is very young, or cannot sit calmly in the dental chair.
duration: treatment usually takes 1 to 3 hours, plus time at the clinic while your child wakes up
tell_doctor: If your child was ill in the past 2 weeks: runny nose, cough, fever
All your child's medicines and allergies
Any problems with anesthesia in your child or relatives
Snoring or pauses in breathing during sleep

prepare.title: Checkup
prepare.text: Before anesthesia, a pediatrician usually checks your child, and tests are needed. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Food and drink
prepare.text: The clinic will tell you the last time for food, milk, and water. Follow it exactly. This matters for safety.

prepare.title: Talk to your child
prepare.text: Tell your child calmly that they will have a nap, and you will be there when they wake up.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes, a spare change of clothes, and a favorite toy.

bring: Your child's documents and your ID
The pediatrician's note and test results
A diaper, spare clothes, and water for afterward
steps: The anesthetist asks you about your child and examines them
Usually you can stay with your child as they fall asleep
Your child falls asleep with a mask or medicine through a vein
The dentist treats the teeth while the anesthetist watches breathing and heart the whole time
Your child wakes up in the recovery room, and you are called in
You rest at the clinic until the doctor lets you go home
feel: After waking, your child may cry, be fussy, or confused. This usually passes quickly
The gums may hurt a little
after: Keep the rest of the day calm, with an adult at home
Drinking and eating when the doctor allows. Start with water and soft food
Watch that your child does not bite their numb lips or cheeks
Come for a follow-up visit when the doctor says
red_flags: Your child has trouble breathing or blue lips: call emergency services
Your child is hard to wake or very floppy: call emergency services
Vomiting several times in a row, or a fever over 38°C (100.4°F)
Bleeding from the mouth that will not stop

faq.q: Is anesthesia dangerous for a child?
faq.a: Modern anesthesia is usually well tolerated. The anesthetist will assess the risks and explain everything.

faq.q: Can I be with my child?
faq.a: Most often yes, while your child falls asleep and wakes up. Check with the clinic.
An empty stomach keeps food from getting into the lungs during sleep.

reminders.text: Your child's dental treatment under anesthesia is tomorrow. Last food and drink strictly at the time the clinic gave you.
